reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must take each operand or word in a WHEN phrase (ANY, condition, TRUE, FALSE, [NOT] identifier/literal/arithmetic expression [THRU ...]) as one selection object, take those joined by ALSO in a single WHEN as one set, and refuse an object form 1985 does not print (partial expression, boolean expression, NOT ANY, NOT TRUE/FALSE).

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry Constructs.EvaluatePartialExpression2002: a partial-expression object (WHEN > 5, WHEN ALPHABETIC) is refused below 2002
DialectBehavior.EvaluateObjectsInWhenPhraseOrder (from 2002): at 85 a function-referencing object is materialized at the statement start

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectLevel|DialectBehavior|ConstructRegistry in EvaluateBinder.cs; the grammar evaluateWhenItem has no edition predicate (later-edition forms are refused in the binder)
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: partial-expression and boolean objects are refused at 85, a literal object may face a literal subject, and a function-referencing object is evaluated before the comparisons
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover NOT placement, signed literal operands and condition-subject forms; ANY across an ALSO set, FALSE subjects with condition objects, NOT ranges and figurative-constant objects are not exercised

probes.printed: A1..A8 OK, EXPECT: MATCH (objects: THRU range, arithmetic M + 4, NOT literal, literal THRU, condition, level-88, TRUE/FALSE, ANY, NOT range, ZERO, SPACES, LOW-VALUE THRU HIGH-VALUE, consecutive WHENs)
error COBOL0900: a partial expression as an EVALUATE selection object requires COBOL-2002
error COBOL3710: ... NOT before the word ANY
probes.expected: refused: NOT is printed only on the operand alternatives

probes.printed: error COBOL3710: ... NOT before the word TRUE
error COBOL1634: subject TRUE and object literal invalid
error COBOL2106: WHEN writes 2 selection objects but 1 subject
probes.expected: refused: a set of objects must match the subjects

reader.notes: SR2 defines a term. The grammar parses one object per ALSO position, and the binder pairs each set with the subjects. The 1985 object list compiled and selected correctly, and every later-edition object form tried was refused at 85 by its construct gate.

refuter.evidence: v1subj.cob S14-S18 (MATCH): NOT condition-name objects against a condition subject, condition objects under a FALSE subject, NOT arithmetic THRU arithmetic, an intrinsic-function object. Refusals at --std 85: TRUE WHEN N -> COBOL1634; N WHEN C1 -> COBOL1634; N WHEN TRUE -> COBOL1634; TRUE WHEN 1 THRU 5 -> COBOL1634; WHEN OTHER before WHEN -> COBOL2073; admitted: N ALSO X WHEN ANY ALSO ANY (OK), X WHEN NOT "AAA" THRU "ABB" (IN), TRUE WHEN NOT N > M (no branch, correct). The sets of objects bind per ALSO position as SR2 defines. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.13.3 SR2.
